When your alert fires, the notification includes a **Summary** and a **Description**. In this milestone, you complete both so anyone who gets the alert can tell what happened and what to check.

Your first alert reported a raw count of 5xx responses. This alert reports a **percentage**, because the query returns a ratio. The Summary uses `printf "%.1f"` to format `$value` as a one-decimal number, and the Description names the ratio explicitly so the on-call reader knows what 5% means.

blocks.targetvalue: QuickPizza error rate at {{ $value | printf "%.1f" }}% over the last 5 minutes
blocks.content: The **Summary** is the first line people see. The `{{ $value }}` template renders the live percentage when the alert fires.

blocks.targetvalue: Fires when the ratio of QuickPizza 5xx responses to total requests exceeds 5% over 5 minutes. Check recent deploys and the app dashboard first.
blocks.content: The **Description** gives more detail than the Summary. Use it to explain what the alert is watching and where to start looking if it goes off.
Your notification now says what happened and what to check. Next, you save and activate the rule.
